topic: The closest-fully-separable-state shape conjecture in arXiv:2209.01430v2, Appendix A.3, equation (A11)
title: Refuting the X-MEMS closest-separable-state conjecture in arXiv:2209.01430v2, Appendix A, Eq. (A11)

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We refute the closest-fully-separable-state shape conjecture of Consiglio, Apollaro and Wieśniak, arXiv:2209.01430v2, Appendix A, Eq. (A11), already for three qubits on the low branch at gamma = 11/112. Every fully separable state of the proposed shape has squared Hilbert–Schmidt distance at least 109/23520, whereas an explicit mixture of ten pure product states has distance 417965512477/90316800000000. The counterexample and exact restricted minimum have self-contained written proofs, as do related counterexamples to the full-separability and concurrence comparisons in the posing source. An elementary bound also establishes its large-qubit limit without the conjectured shape.
summary: An exact ten-product-state mixture beats the entire conjectured three-qubit closest-state family. Written corollaries separate PPT from full separability, disprove two-qubit concurrence comparisons, establish exact multipartite comparison failures and prove a general corner-coherence limit.
